question: Sheep pox and goat pox have remained endemic in Greece since 2023, with continuous outbreaks mainly found in Macedonia and Thrace. Despite containment measures and the mass killing of herds, the disease continues to spread. This has severe repercussions for livestock farming, the rural economy and social cohesion in the affected areas.

DG SANTE’s report (of 16 May 2025) highlights the insufficient administrative capacity of the Greek authorities, the difficulties in monitoring restricted zones and the risk of further spread. In accordance with Article 12 of Regulation (EU) 2020/687 and Article 69 of Regulation (EU) 2016/429, Member States may postpone the killing of listed animals and implement a vaccination plan.

Nevertheless, the Greek Government argues that sheep pox and goat pox vaccines are not authorised, citing national legislation which still sets out the killing of animals as a key measure. Conversely, the European Commission and DG SANTE explicitly refer to vaccination strategies and making use of the European vaccine bank for category A diseases. Can the Commission say: 1.
Are authorised sheep pox and goat pox vaccines available, and in what quantities?
What measures will be taken to ensure that Greece complies with EU law, which permits vaccination as an alternative to killing?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.3.2026) As referred to in the reply to E-004261/20251, there is currently no approved sheep and goat pox (SGP) vaccine in the EU. Nonetheless, the Veterinary Medicinal Products Regulation2 allows Member States’ competent authorities to use a vaccine not authorised within the Union.

To date Greece has been implementing the mandatory SGP control measures laid down in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/6873 as well as the measures laid down in Commission Implementing Decision 2024/22074 including the immediate killing of all animals of listed species in the affected establishments, along with biosecurity measures and establishment of specific restricted zones.
Vaccination against SGP is not mandatory. The decision to implement SGP vaccination rests with the competent authorities of the MS concerned in line with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/3615.

The Commission (along with EU Veterinary Emergency Team6 experts) has repeatedly indicated the need to consider vaccination as a supplementary control measure for SGP, in view of the current epidemiological situation and is doing everything within its power to support Greece in reaching a decision on this.
In case Greece decides to implement SGP vaccination, the Commission can also arrange the donation of vaccines from the EU SGP vaccine bank, upon request.
